attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both the annual figures and the 'vastly more cash' comparison with both named rivals.

contract.note: Reading Google as Alphabet, profit as net income and a June 30 cash snapshot is fair and ordinary. The result depends on how 'vastly' is read and on the contract keeping the accounting basis unknown, which is cautious given the exact match.

evidence.note: Audited 2025 revenue of $402.8B and net income of $132.2B match the stated figures closely. The contract keeps the basis unknown, so I treat this as context and do not let it decide the result on its own.
Alphabet held $242.5B in cash and short-term securities at June 30, 2026. That is only one side of the comparison.
Anthropic held about $131.7B at June 30, 2026, filed before the cutoff. Alphabet has roughly 1.8x as much, which makes 'vastly' doubtful but does not settle it.
This is a press estimate of OpenAI's cash at March 31 (over $73B), not June 30, so it is the wrong period for the contract.

reviews.rationale: The annual figures match Alphabet's 2025 10-K. But the cash part is not settled: there is no June OpenAI balance, and against Anthropic's ~$132B, Alphabet's $242.5B is only about 1.8x, which falls short of what 'vastly' plainly suggests. The contract also sets no ratio. With one component settled and the other open, the combined claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps all three assertions about competitors.

contract.note: Reading 'talent pool' as AI research depth and using July as the period are reasonable. Since the speaker named no reputation measure, which survey is used matters.

evidence.note: Caliber's monthly scores fall from 60 to a July low of 53. The August rebound comes after the target period.
A July 27 court notice in Anthropic v. Department of War shows active litigation with the administration.

reviews.rationale: Two of the three parts hold: OpenAI's reputation fell through July, and Anthropic was in active litigation with the administration. No evidence measures Microsoft's or Amazon's AI talent depth against Google's. The contract needs all three parts, so the combined claim is unresolved.

semantics.note: 'Great' is rendered as 'strong'; the named products are kept as illustrations.

contract.note: The plain reading (very large existing audiences plus practical routes to deliver features) is fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: Company disclosure, June 2026: Gemini runs in 13 products with over a billion users each, and AI Overviews has over 2.5B monthly users.
Company disclosure, May 2026: Android described as reaching billions. This is qualitative but in period.
Company disclosure, April 2026: Workspace integrations including Gmail and Docs, with over 3B Workspace users.
Company disclosure: over 140M users engaged with Ask YouTube in June 2026, an AI feature delivered through YouTube.

reviews.rationale: Dated company disclosures from April to June 2026 show billion-scale audiences across Search, Android, Workspace and YouTube, plus actual AI integrations within them. These are company disclosures, but the contract accepts that source type, and no counterevidence appears.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' makes this a forecast. The historical 'over a decade' clause is split off and left unscored, which is acceptable.

contract.note: No deadline was given. Requiring actual collaboration rather than announced intent is fair, but whether advisory work counts as collaboration is an interpretation.

evidence.note: Google's August 5 announcement says Hassabis will stay closely connected and advise. This is intent before publication, not evidence of later collaboration.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet has no dated record of substantive collaboration after publication and no record of a definitive break, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The announcement shows only intent, and the forecast stays unresolved.
